figures.finding: Cyprus's film scheme gives a cash rebate of up to 45% of eligible spend in Cyprus, set by the production's cultural-test score and paid after filming on an audited report, or instead a tax credit on the same criteria limited to 50% of the company's taxable income a year (carried forward up to five years), plus VAT refunds and an equipment-investment deduction; the Cyprus Film Commission, chaired by Invest Cyprus with the Ministries of Finance and of Education and Culture and the Deputy Ministry of Tourism, decides.

value.paid: after filming, on receipt and review of the audit report

figures.applies: Republic of Cyprus; feature films, TV series, documentaries, animation; 2026-11-01.

sources.said: Rebate of up to 45% of eligible expenditures incurred in Cyprus will be granted, where the amount will depend on the score of the production at the cultural test. The rebate will be given once filming is completed, on receipt of the audit report and its review by the committee. … The sum of the tax credit against the taxable income shall not exceed 50% of the Applicants’ taxable income for the tax year within which the production is made. … shall be carried forward and be given within the next five years … The aid may not exceed 20% of the qualifying production expenditures in the case of small enterprises and 10% of the qualifying production expenditures in the case of medium-sized enterprises. … The Cyprus Film Commission, chaired by Invest Cyprus is the responsible body for the examination of applications. The Commission consists, of the following Ministries and Organisations: Invest Cyprus Ministry of Finance Ministry of Education and Culture Deputy Ministry of Tourism

figures.finding: The Deputy Ministry of Culture paid more than EUR 2.5 million from its Film Production budget line to ten production companies in 2025, the largest single award EUR 525,875; separately it gave EUR 405,000 to five minority co-productions in 2025 on the Cinema Advisory Committee's (SEKIN) recommendation. No published per-film cap or share was reached.

value.body: Deputy Ministry of Culture (Cinema Advisory Committee, SEKIN)
